$comment: Inline-asm P20: the FIRST runnable witness that `asm goto` lowers at all. ★★★ BORN AGAINST A REFUSAL, NOT A MISCOMPILE: ✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI immediately before this cycle, every statement in main.c failed the build with `L0001 … an assembly operand binding carries a register and no BLOCK — so a label target cannot be expressed`. Four independent defects had to close for this file to exist, and each SHAPE is the discriminating witness for one of them, so none of them is redundant: SHAPE 1 is the FALL-THROUGH edge (the MIR terminator used to record successors = the LABELS ONLY, and the statements after the asm were built into a block hir_to_mir called dead which the mandatory unreachable-prune then DELETED — ✔MEASURED on gcc 13.3.0, clang 19.1.1 and aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0 that `asm goto` FALLS THROUGH when its template does not branch); SHAPE 2 is the POSITIONAL label reference `%l2`, carrying one output and one input on purpose because the two candidate index bases AGREE at zero operands and diverge the moment one exists; SHAPE 3 is the SYMBOLIC operand name `%[in]`, refused outright before this cycle with `'%[in]' names neither a register this target declares nor one of the 2 operand(s) bound`; SHAPE 4 is an `asm goto` used as a LOOP LATCH, which is the only shape here that carries phis on a multi-successor asm block; SHAPE 5 carries THREE labels beside two operands so that the index base is FALSIFIABLE rather than merely checked — `%l2` is the FIRST label under the source's base and the THIRD under a labels-only one, both spellings exist under both readings, so a wrong base does not refuse, it BRANCHES SOMEWHERE ELSE and returns 33 instead of 11 (✔MEASURED with `mintTemplateSpellings`' base forced to 0). ★★ THE `release` ARM IS WHERE SHAPE 4 EARNS ITS PLACE. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-19 with `InlineAsmGoto` removed from `terminatorOwnsEverySuccessorBranch`, this file against a copy of ITSELF carrying every shape but SHAPE 4: this file exits 1 at release and 42 at the baseline, while the SHAPE-4-less copy exits 42 at BOTH — so shape 4 is the sole discriminator for that guard and only the release arm sees it. The phi-destination copies for the back edge are placed inline BEFORE the terminator under the mutant and then run on the EXIT edge too (the lost-copy miscompile). A baseline-only corpus would have shipped it green. ⚠ THE `volatile` SEEDS ARE LOAD-BEARING: without them release folds each branch condition to a constant before lowering and the `asm goto` stops being a branch, leaving the example exiting 42 while testing nothing. ⚠ WHY THE aarch64 ARM USES `long`: `%w0` is an operand MODIFIER (a narrower VIEW of the bound register) and no shipped target declares a width-view vocabulary for it, so the semantic tier refuses it fail-loud rather than running the operand at the wrong width — the same note and the same reason as `c_inline_asm_operands`. ⚠ WHY SHAPE 2's OUTPUT IS READ ON THE FALL-THROUGH PATH: the reference measurement settled ACCEPTANCE of an `asm goto` output read on the jump path but not its validity, and an example must not pin behaviour its own references leave open.
